questions.stem: The Centre recently released states an additional instalment of tax devolution of over Rs 1.09 lakh crore. In this context, consider the following statements regarding tax devolution to states in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The share of central taxes devolved to states is decided by the Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution.
The 15th Finance Commission recommended that 41% of the net proceeds of central divisible pool taxes be devolved to states.
Tax devolution to states is distinct from, and in addition to, grants-in-aid provided under Article 275.
The vertical devolution share recommended by the Finance Commission is legally binding on Parliament and cannot be altered during annual budgeting.
questions.explanation: Statements 1-3 are correct: the Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 every five years, the 15th Finance Commission recommended a 41% vertical devolution share (reduced from 42% after J&K's reorganisation into Union Territories), and tax devolution is distinct from Article 275 grants-in-aid. Statement 4 is incorrect since Finance Commission recommendations are advisory in nature and not constitutionally binding on Parliament, though conventionally accepted.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: States get addition instalment of tax devolution of ₹1.09 lakh crore, supported by strong economy, taxes—See break-up
questions.pyqLink: Tests Finance Commission's constitutional basis and vertical devolution — analogous to UPSC prelims questions on Article 280 and Finance Commission functions.

questions.stem: India's October GST collections grew sharply, drawing attention to the GST framework. Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The GST Council is constituted under Article 279A of the Constitution and is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
GST collections comprise Central GST (CGST), State GST (SGST), Integrated GST (IGST) and a Compensation Cess on select goods.
Under the destination-based consumption principle, IGST revenue on inter-state trade is retained by the exporting state rather than the importing state.
The current GST rate structure has only two slabs of 5% and 18%, with no additional rate for any category of goods.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A chaired by the Union Finance Minister, and GST revenue is split across CGST, SGST, IGST and Compensation Cess. Statement 3 is wrong because GST is destination-based — IGST accrues to the importing/consuming state, not the exporting state. Statement 4 is wrong because the recent rate rationalisation retained a higher 40% slab for select demerit and luxury goods alongside the two main slabs.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India's October Gross GST collections jump 22.9% to Rs 2.31 lakh crore
questions.pyqLink: Tests GST Council composition and rate structure — similar to UPSC prelims questions on GST Council powers under Article 279A.

questions.stem: With reference to India's crude oil import dependence, highlighted amid continuing disruption from the West Asia conflict, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: India imports nearly 90% of its crude oil requirement, making it vulnerable to global supply disruptions.
India's crude oil import basket is sourced entirely from OPEC member countries, with no imports from non-OPEC producers such as Russia or the United States.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — India depends on imports for close to 90% of its crude oil needs, exposing it to price shocks from conflicts in supplier regions. Statement 2 is incorrect because Russia (a non-OPEC producer) alone accounted for roughly 55% of a major Indian refiner's crude basket, with the Middle East, Africa, Brazil and the US/Venezuela making up the rest.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: IOC says crude Q2 price volatile as procurement swings between discounts and premiums
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's energy security and import diversification — a recurring theme in UPSC prelims on crude oil sourcing and strategic petroleum reserves.

questions.stem: With reference to the El Niño phenomenon and its effect on the Indian monsoon, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: El Niño refers to the periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean.
A strong El Niño year always results in a below-normal Indian southwest monsoon, with no exceptions recorded historically.
The India Meteorological Department is the nodal agency responsible for issuing the official monsoon forecast for India.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: El Niño is the warming of Pacific sea surface temperatures, and the IMD is India's nodal monsoon-forecasting agency. Statement 2 is false — as the 1997 case shows, one of the strongest El Niños of the 20th century still produced a nearly normal monsoon, demonstrating that El Niño is only one of several factors (including the Indian Ocean Dipole) influencing monsoon outcomes.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
questions.pyqLink: Tests ENSO mechanics and monsoon variability — similar to UPSC prelims questions on El Niño/La Niña and their link to Indian monsoon.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs regarding the mechanism of the Indian monsoon:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon
Heavy rainfall along the Western Ghats and Konkan coast
Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon
Primary source of rainfall for the Western Rajasthan desert region
Principal rainy season for the Tamil Nadu coast
Primary driver of India's southwest monsoon rainfall
questions.explanation: Only pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched: the Arabian Sea branch brings heavy orographic rainfall to the Western Ghats/Konkan coast, and the retreating north-east monsoon is indeed Tamil Nadu's main rainy season. Pair 2 is wrong because the Bay of Bengal branch feeds North-East India and the Gangetic plains, not the arid Western Rajasthan region. Pair 4 is wrong because western disturbances are extratropical systems causing winter/pre-monsoon rainfall in north-west India, not the driver of the southwest monsoon.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
questions.pyqLink: Tests the branches and mechanism of the southwest monsoon — a recurring static-geography theme in UPSC prelims.

questions.stem: With reference to the legal requirement for operating wireless transmitting devices such as walkie-talkies in India, which one of the following best describes the regulatory position?
options: Any wireless communication device can be freely operated without authorization once legally purchased, since ownership itself constitutes permission to transmit.

Operating a wireless transmitting device requires a licence or authorization under the Indian Telegraph/Wireless Telegraphy framework administered by the Wireless Planning and Coordination (WPC) Wing of the Department of Telecommunications, except in specific license-exempt frequency bands.
Only devices manufactured domestically require licensing, while imported wireless devices are exempt from spectrum authorization.
Licensing for wireless transmitting devices in India is governed exclusively by state governments under the Police Act, with no central regulatory role.
questions.explanation: The correct position is option 2: the WPC Wing of the Department of Telecommunications administers spectrum allocation and equipment licensing under the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 and the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, with certain low-power, short-range bands kept license-exempt. Option 1 wrongly equates purchase with authorization to transmit; option 3 wrongly ties licensing to country of manufacture; option 4 wrongly removes the central government's statutory role, which is actually primary, not state-governed.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: You can buy a walkie-talkie online. But can you legally use it?
questions.pyqLink: A 'best describes the term' format analogous to UPSC's Merchant Discount Rate-style questions, here applied to spectrum/wireless-licensing regulation.

questions.stem: With reference to the government's revision of export duties on petrol, diesel and ATF, consider the following two statements:
statements: Statement-I: India periodically revises export duties (including a windfall/special additional excise duty) on fuel exports when global crude oil prices rise sharply due to geopolitical disruptions.

Statement-II: Such a duty is designed to capture the additional profit margins refiners earn from exporting fuel at elevated international prices, thereby discouraging diversion of fuel away from the domestic market.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: the government has been conducting fortnightly reviews of export duties on diesel and ATF (and earlier petrol) since global crude prices spiked due to the West Asia conflict. Statement-II correctly explains this — the windfall/special additional excise duty is meant to tax the extraordinary export margins refiners earn when international prices surge, and to keep adequate fuel available for domestic consumption rather than being diverted abroad for higher profit.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Govt scraps export duty on petrol; hikes levies on diesel, ATF — check details here
questions.pyqLink: Tests the rationale of windfall taxation on fuel exports — conceptually parallel to UPSC's Statement-I/Statement-II format introduced from 2022 on economic policy rationale.

questions.stem: With reference to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: GST is a destination-based tax levied on the consumption of goods and services, and Integrated GST (IGST) is levied on inter-State supplies and imports.
The GST Council, constituted under Article 279-A of the Constitution, is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
questions.explanation: GST is indeed a destination-based consumption tax, and IGST applies to inter-State supplies and imports, with revenue apportioned between Centre and the destination State. Statement 2 is wrong: the GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not the Home Minister; it includes the Union Finance Minister, the Union Minister of State for Finance, and State Finance/Taxation Ministers.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: GST mop-up surges 23% to second-highest level of ₹2.31 lakh crore in October on festive demand boost
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 279-A GST Council composition and the destination-based tax principle, similar to UPSC 2017/2018 questions on GST Council structure.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's satellite navigation and launch vehicle programme:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) is designed to provide positioning services over the Indian landmass and a region extending about 1,500 km around it.
The first-generation IRNSS satellites carried only indigenously developed atomic clocks.
The GSLV employs an indigenously developed cryogenic upper stage, unlike the PSLV.
The Department of Space, under which ISRO functions, is under the direct charge of the Prime Minister.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct: NavIC's stated coverage is India plus ~1,500 km around it; GSLV uses an indigenous cryogenic stage (CE-7.5) while PSLV does not; and the Department of Space reports directly to the Prime Minister. Statement 2 is false — the first-generation IRNSS satellites used imported (Swiss) atomic clocks, and it is only the second-generation NVS satellites that carry indigenous clocks, as noted in the article.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Slow recovery: On the ISRO's GSLV-F18 mission
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional structure of ISRO/Department of Space and NavIC design parameters, similar to UPSC's recurring questions on IRNSS/NavIC coverage and GSLV vs PSLV technology.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding medical education regulation in India:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The National Medical Commission (NMC) was constituted under the National Medical Commission Act, 2019, replacing the Medical Council of India.
The NMC is a constitutional body established under Article 323-B of the Constitution of India.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) functions as an attached office of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — the NMC replaced the MCI under the 2019 Act. Statement 3 is correct — DGHS is an attached office of the MoHFW, as reflected in the Delhi High Court directing both NMC and DGHS to jointly inquire. Statement 2 is false: the NMC is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament, not a constitutional body; Article 323-B merely empowers Parliament to set up tribunals for certain matters and has no bearing on the NMC.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Delhi High Court seeks report on qualifications of two doctors accused of mishandling child
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory vs constitutional body distinction, a recurring UPSC theme (e.g., UPSC questions distinguishing NHRC, CIC, NMC as statutory bodies from constitutional bodies like CAG, UPSC).

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs regarding coal usage and regulation in the power and industrial sectors:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Mixing imported coal with domestic coal to meet calorific and operational requirements at domestic coal-based (DCB) power plants
Primarily used as an input for the steel industry owing to its low-ash, caking properties
Issued by the Ministry of Coal to mandate use of coal combustion residue in cement and brick manufacturing
A statutory requirement for all thermal power plants under the Coal Mines (Conservation and Development) Act, 1974
questions.explanation: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched: DCB plants import coal for blending, and coking coal is the key steel-sector input, as stated in the article. Pair 3 is wrong — the fly ash utilisation notification is issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not the Ministry of Coal. Pair 4 is wrong — CCS is not a statutory requirement under the 1974 Act, which deals with conservation of coal resources, not emission capture technology.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: India's coal imports decline 5.83% in August
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional responsibility for coal-related environmental regulation, in the spirit of UPSC's pairs-matched questions on schemes/notifications and their issuing ministries.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's coal reserves and coalfields:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: India's major coking coal reserves are concentrated in the Jharia and Bokaro coalfields of Jharkhand.
The Raniganj coalfield, India's oldest coal mining region, is located in Jharkhand.
Most of India's coal reserves are of Tertiary age and are concentrated in the north-eastern states.
Lignite reserves in India are predominantly found in Tamil Nadu, followed by Rajasthan and Gujarat.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: Jharia and Bokaro in Jharkhand hold major coking coal reserves, and Tamil Nadu (Neyveli) leads in lignite reserves, followed by Rajasthan and Gujarat. Statement 2 is wrong — Raniganj is located in West Bengal, not Jharkhand. Statement 3 is wrong — most Indian coal is of Gondwana (Permian) age found in peninsular river valleys like the Damodar; Tertiary coal is a minor share, confined mainly to the north-east.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Coal India's production increases 19% as mining recovers after monsoon slump
questions.pyqLink: Tests the geography of mineral resources — Gondwana vs Tertiary coal and major coalfields — a staple of UPSC's physical/economic geography questions on mineral distribution.

questions.stem: With reference to a Geographical Indication (GI) tag in India, which one of the following best describes the term?
options: It is a form of intellectual property right that identifies a good as originating from a definite geographical territory, possessing qualities or a reputation attributable to that origin, registered under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999.
It is a certification mark granted by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to agricultural produce meeting prescribed safety standards.
It is a patent granted under the Patents Act, 1970, protecting the process of cultivation of an indigenous crop variety.
It is a trademark registered by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare to promote export of heritage food products.
questions.explanation: A GI tag is an intellectual property right under the 1999 Act (administered by the GI Registry under the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks), linking a product's distinct qualities to its geographical origin — relevant to the article's call for GI-tagged value chains for heritage produce. It is not an FSSAI safety certification, a patent, or a trademark administered by the Agriculture Ministry — each confuses GI with a different IP or regulatory instrument.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Can India's heritage produce find a place on the global food map?
questions.pyqLink: Tests the legal nature of GI tags, a recurring UPSC theme (e.g., UPSC 2019 question on 'Merchant Discount Rate' style best-describes format applied here to GI tagging of Darjeeling Tea, Basmati Rice, etc.)

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the recent $6.3 billion theft from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance:
statements: Statement-I: The theft has been linked by investigators to actors associated with North Korea.

Statement-II: UN Panel of Experts reports have found that North Korea uses proceeds from cryptocurrency theft to fund its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programmes, circumventing UN Security Council sanctions.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct — the article notes the breach was linked to North Korea. Statement-II is a well-documented pattern verified by UN Panel of Experts reports, explaining the motive behind such state-linked cyber-heists: sanctions-evasion to fund weapons programmes. Statement-II thus correctly explains why North Korea-linked actors target crypto exchanges, making it the explanation for Statement-I.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Binance sees outflows stabilising as exchange returns online after $6.3 billion heist
questions.pyqLink: Tests UN Security Council sanctions regime on North Korea and its circumvention via cryptocurrency, relevant to UPSC's growing focus on non-traditional security and international sanctions regimes.

questions.stem: With reference to the investigative jurisdiction of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The CBI can investigate a case referred to it by a State's police only after that State has granted "general consent" under the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946.
The Supreme Court's power to direct a CBI investigation without the concerned State's consent is derived from its appellate jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the CBI, being a police force for the Union Territories extended to the States, needs the concerned State's "general" or "case-specific" consent under Section 6 of the DSPE Act, 1946 to investigate there. Statement 2 is incorrect: when constitutional courts order a CBI probe without State consent, the power flows from the Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 32 (or the High Court's under Article 226), not from the appellate/special-leave jurisdiction under Article 136.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: SC disposes of Ram Temple embezzlement petitions after Uttar Pradesh says charge sheet filed
questions.pyqLink: Tests CBI's status under the DSPE Act, 1946 and the constitutional basis for courts ordering a CBI probe without state consent; similar to UPSC Prelims questions on the CBI's statutory and constitutional status.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding poverty measurement:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The World Bank's current International Poverty Line for extreme poverty is set at $3 per day in 2021 Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) terms.
India's Multidimensional Poverty Index is released by the Reserve Bank of India using data from the National Family Health Survey.
The World Bank's Lower-Middle-Income Country poverty line is set at a higher dollar-per-day value than its extreme poverty line.
The World Bank's Poverty and Equity Brief projects India's poverty rate, measured at the Lower-Middle-Income Country threshold, to rise between 2026 and 2028.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the World Bank's extreme poverty line is $3/day (2021 PPP), lower than its Lower-Middle-Income Country line of $4.2/day. Statement 2 is wrong because India's Multidimensional Poverty Index is released by NITI Aayog, not the RBI. Statement 4 is wrong because the Poverty and Equity Brief projects the LMIC-threshold poverty rate to fall further, from 14.2% in 2026 to 12.1% by 2028.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India's poverty rate has fallen, but challenges remain: Jobs, AI, ageing population
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static distinction between World Bank PPP-based poverty lines and India's NITI Aayog-administered Multidimensional Poverty Index; similar to UPSC Prelims questions on the MPI.

questions.stem: With reference to NavIC, which one of the following best describes it?
options: It is a satellite-based augmentation system that corrects GPS signal errors for civil aviation over Indian airspace
It is a constellation of geostationary communication satellites used exclusively for disaster-warning dissemination
It is an Indian regional satellite navigation system providing position, navigation and timing services over India and a region extending about 1,500 km beyond its boundary
It is India's global positioning system, comprising satellites in polar sun-synchronous orbit, offering worldwide coverage comparable to GPS
questions.explanation: NavIC (formerly IRNSS) is a regional, not global, satellite navigation system built from satellites in geostationary and geosynchronous orbits, covering India and an area extending roughly 1,500 km beyond its borders. Option (a) describes GAGAN, India's satellite-based augmentation system for aviation, not NavIC. Option (b) describes communication/meteorological satellites like INSAT, not a navigation constellation. Option (d) is wrong because NavIC is regional and does not use polar sun-synchronous orbits.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Why ISRO's latest success matters more than it appears | The Hindu Editorial
questions.pyqLink: Tests the distinction between NavIC/IRNSS, GAGAN and GPS; similar to past Prelims questions distinguishing India's satellite navigation and augmentation systems.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the "Classical Language" status conferred on Indian languages:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Kannada was among the early languages, after Tamil and Sanskrit, to be granted "Classical Language" status by the Government of India, in 2008, alongside Telugu.

One of the criteria for classical language status is that the language must possess a body of ancient literature, aged between 1,500 and 2,000 years, that is not borrowed from another speech community.
The decision to confer classical language status is formally taken by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, based on the recommendation of a Linguistic Experts Committee.
questions.explanation: All three statements are correct. Tamil (2004) and Sanskrit (2005) were the first languages declared classical, followed by Telugu and Kannada in 2008. The criteria include high antiquity (1,500-2,000 years) and an original, non-borrowed literary tradition. The Ministry of Culture takes the final decision based on recommendations of a Linguistic Experts Committee, not the Sahitya Akademi, which is only a literary body and not a statutory decision-making authority for this purpose.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Dr. Rajkumar's song 'If You Come Today' gets a hip-hop twist, courtesy rapper Gubbi
questions.pyqLink: Tests the criteria and conferring authority for Classical Language status; similar to UPSC Prelims questions listing India's classical languages.

questions.stem: With reference to the physical geography of peninsular India and tropical cyclones, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Rayalaseema's comparatively low rainfall is primarily attributed to its location in the rain shadow of the Himalayas, which blocks moisture-laden winds from reaching it.
Tropical cyclones rarely form within about 5 degrees latitude of the equator because the Coriolis force, essential for imparting rotation to the storm system, is negligible there.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct: the Coriolis force, which deflects winds and imparts the cyclonic rotation, is near zero at the equator and strengthens with latitude, so tropical cyclones almost never form within about 5 degrees of it. Statement 1 is incorrect: Rayalaseema's aridity is an interior, rain-shadow effect linked to the Eastern Ghats and its distance from both the southwest and northeast monsoon moisture sources, not the Himalayas, which lie far to the north and play no role in this region's rainfall.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Rain begins in north Andhra ahead of Cyclone Murasu
questions.pyqLink: Tests conditions favourable for tropical cyclone formation and the rain-shadow concept; similar to UPSC Prelims questions on conditions necessary for cyclone formation over warm tropical oceans.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of low-pressure weather systems over the Indian seas, as classified by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), and their associated sustained wind speeds:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Three pairs are correctly matched: Depression (31-49 km/h), Cyclonic Storm (62-88 km/h), and Severe Cyclonic Storm (89-117 km/h) match IMD's standard classification, consistent with Cyclone Murasu being termed a "severe cyclonic storm" with winds of 100-110 km/h. The fourth pair is wrong: a wind speed of 118-165 km/h corresponds to a "Very Severe Cyclonic Storm," while a "Super Cyclonic Storm" requires sustained winds exceeding 220 km/h.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Cyclone Murasu LIVE updates: Odisha expedites evacuation from vulnerable areas as storm intensifies
questions.pyqLink: Tests IMD's wind-speed-based classification of cyclonic disturbances; similar to UPSC Prelims questions on cyclone categorisation and naming conventions.
